column1: # What the resource-control suite (suite.sh, unpriv.sh) must report. One row per behaviour, tab separated:
#   id  area  resource  envs  fact  expectation  description
# envs are the environments the row applies to; the judge (resctl-judge.py) expands it to one row "<id>.<env>" per
# environment and reads the fact "<prefix><fact>" of that environment's session:
#   unpriv  u_  the unprivileged session (a user namespace: no cgroup hierarchy, builds and tests the crate)
#   host    h_  the real root of this host, lifecycle auto (limits through the hierarchy that has the controller)
#   hostv1  v_  the same host with the cgroup v1 freezer forced as the lifecycle backend; it runs only the sections that
#               depend on that backend (layout normal isolation terminate recover lifecycle): the limits, throttle and
#               pressure rows read the same v1 resource hierarchies as host, and pressure has no v1 source at all
#   guest   g_  the cgroup v2 test bed guest (cgroup_no_v1=all): the layout the host cannot offer
#   bed         the facts of the guest session itself (QEMU, boot): no prefix
# A fact may be covered once per environment; every fact an environment reports must be covered, and every row must
# have its fact. `area` is the section of the suite (what is being exercised), `resource` the domain being controlled:
#   memory cpu processes io lifecycle protection (the system domain outside every kill domain) policy platform
# Expectations are those of tools-test/inventory.tsv: ok | =VALUE | ~REGEX | deny:REGEX (a refusal that is expected).
# A failing row is a LIMIT only through an entry of limits.tsv (a measured cause plus a passing guest proof).
# ---- build: the crate builds clean and its unit tests pass inside the session
